evidence.excerpt:
Zero-shot Neural Architecture Search removes the prohibitive cost of traditional NAS, but its search
process is typically based on the evolutionary algorithm (EA); lacking an explicit model of the objective,
it often resorts to a near-random search through mutation. Bayesian Optimization offers a principled
alternative by modeling the objective and aggregating information across iterations, but scales poorly to
the high-dimensional, discrete, graph-structured spaces of modern NAS, restricting its use to only small
networks. In this paper, we bring Bayesian Optimization to zero-shot NAS for large-scale architectures
by learning a latent space via a Variational Autoencoder trained to reconstruct a novel prefix encoding
of architectures and propose a proxy scalarization that combines several zero-shot proxies into a single
Bayesian Optimization objective. After only 10,000 iterations of

expressed by prefix encoding that serializes each architecture block into a compact, bijective string over
a vocabulary of primitive and compound operations. The resulting latent space provides a smooth, low-
dimensional representation of large-scale heterogeneous architectures suitable as the search domain for
Bayesian Optimization.

The search is seeded from the union of three complementary architecture pools - randomly grown graphs,
random-walk graphs, and mutation-perturbed graphs—designed to provide broad initial coverage of the
design space. We sampleKseed = 256 architectures uniformly from this union and evaluate the scalarized
zero-shot proxy (see Section 4.1). The resulting scores are used to fit the scalarizer statistics µ and Σ (Eq. 3)
once; these are frozen for the remainder of the search. Each seed architecture is encoded to its deterministic
posterior mean µϕ(s) and inserted into the BO observation set together with its penalized composite score.
We run the process for 10 000 iterations, resulting in a total 8 GPU hours.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The selected architecture is trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K and fine-tuned on MS-COCO and ADE20K, with reported top-1 accuracy, AP, and mIoU compared against established baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth validation accuracy after full training on ImageNet-1K and downstream task metrics on MS-COCO and ADE20K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Scalarized zero-shot proxy scores from whitened VKDNW components with a parameter-count penalty.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of achieving competitive zero-shot NAS performance (81.51% top-1 ImageNet-1K at ~27M parameters) and cross-task generalization align well with the empirical training results and comparative tables.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The authors evaluate the single top-selected architecture by fully training it on ImageNet-1K under the standard UniNAS recipe, transferring it to COCO object detection/segmentation and ADE20K semantic segmentation, and providing component ablations covering latent space, prefix encoding, and proxy scalarization.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Full training and standard task metric evaluation (top-1 classification accuracy, AP, and mIoU) on standard benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Actual ground-truth validation accuracy following complete training from scratch on ImageNet-1K, MS-COCO, and ADE20K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Scalarized zero-shot training-free proxy scores (whitened VKDNW multi-dimensional components) penalized by parameter deviation.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the proxy scalarizer covariance is frozen after initialization rather than adaptively recalibrated, and that latent decoding requires retry perturbation for occasional invalid shape matching.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the 20-node compound prefix grammar, the graph convolutional encoder and autoregressive transformer decoder with soft-DTW loss, the multi-proxy whitening scalarization, and budget-penalized GP-based Bayesian optimization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, novel system that scales BO to expressive NAS spaces via a grammar-constrained latent space, with robust full-training verification on standard vision benchmarks and solid ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces a Bayesian Optimization approach for zero-shot neural architecture search over large-scale spaces by learning a continuous latent space with a VAE operating on a prefix encoding of architecture graphs, coupled with a Mahalanobis-whitened proxy scalarization.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, novel system that scales BO to expressive NAS spaces via a grammar-constrained latent space, with robust full-training verification on standard vision benchmarks and solid ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge that the proxy scalarizer covariance is frozen after initialization rather than adaptively recalibrated, and that latent decoding requires retry perturbation for occasional invalid shape matching.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
